title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). X is an oriented surface. A discrete group G acts properly on X. The stabilizers preserve orientation and act faithfully near their fixed points. Y = X/G carries the ramification signature d. X^! is the set of points with nontrivial stabilizer, and Y^! = Supp d is its image. The orbifold fundamental group π = π1((X,G),x) is identified with π1((Y,d),y) by isomorphism (1). For each b in Y^!, the 'truncated loop' homomorphism (2) is an outer homomorphism T_b ⊗ Z/d_b → π', where T_b is the free rank-1 module of 'twisted integers'. For a over b, the stabilizer G_a is canonically isomorphic to T_a ⊗ Z/d_a (equation (4)).

This page.

1. The orbifold group sits in the extension (5): 1 → π1(X,x) → π1((X,G),x) → G → 1. This is the fundamental-group extension of the Borel construction X_hG (cf. §15).

2. Each point a gives a π1(X)-conjugacy class of splittings k_a : G_a → π1((X,G)) of (5) over G_a. Concretely, k_a is the map on fundamental groups induced by the inclusion of the orbit G·a ≅ G/G_a (homotopy BG_a) into X_hG.

3. Claim, for X ≠ S^2 and a finite subgroup G_0 ⊂ G: π1(X)-conjugacy classes of splittings over G_0 correspond bijectively to fixed points of G_0 on X. This is the discrete, topological 'section conjecture' for group actions on aspherical surfaces. It is classical, via Smith theory or Nielsen/Kerckhoff realization: on a hyperbolic or flat surface, a finite cyclic group of isometries fixes a point, and distinct fixed points give non-conjugate lifts.

4. Passing to outer homomorphisms (conjugation by all of π) gives a bijection between the following two sets:
   - outer liftings of the inclusion G_0 ⊂ G (letting G_0 vary in its conjugacy class);
   - G-orbits in X^!, i.e. points of Y^!.

5. Proposition. There is a bijection between Y^! and the 'maximal' outer homomorphisms φ_b : Γ → π that lift inclusions Γ ⊂ G with Γ ≠ 1. Such Γ are necessarily cyclic; they are exactly the stabilizers G_a for a over b.
   - In modern terms, Y^! is in bijection with the conjugacy classes of maximal finite subgroups of the orbifold fundamental group (a Fuchsian group when X is hyperbolic). Each such subgroup is cyclic of order d_b, generated by the elliptic element around the cone point.
   - The next page adds compatibility (7): composing (4), φ_b and (1) recovers the truncated loop map (2).
   - It then begins comparing cusp inertia T_a → π1(X) with T_b → π1(Y). This feeds the explicit determination of the isomorphism π'_{0,3} ≅ 𝔖^+_{0,3} for the cartographic groups.
errors: The stated 1-1 correspondence between outer homomorphisms 'lifting the inclusion G_0 ⊂ G' and G-orbits in X^! is slightly imprecise. Modulo conjugation by all of π, the image subgroup G_0 moves within its G-conjugacy class. For a fixed G_0, the correct statement is a bijection with orbits of the normalizer N_G(G_0) on Fix(G_0). The Proposition, restricted to maximal Γ and taken up to conjugation, is the correct form.

The exception X ≠ S^2 is the right one under the orientation hypotheses: there π1(X) = 1, so the two fixed points of a rotation give the same splitting. For non-proper or orientation-reversing actions further care would be needed, but these are excluded by hypothesis.
Non-maximal nontrivial Γ ⊂ G_a are legitimately excluded. Their splittings are restrictions of the maximal ones, which is why 'maximal' is needed for the bijection with Y^!.

ideas.what: Orbifold fundamental group of a G-surface as extension of G by π1(X) (homotopy quotient X_hG)
ideas.modern_name: orbifold fundamental group / equivariant fundamental group, Borel construction
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thurston (orbifolds, 1970s); Haefliger; classical Fuchsian group theory
ideas.where_published: SGA1 (étale analogue); La Longue Marche à travers la théorie de Galois (1981), §15

ideas.what: Conjugacy classes of splittings of 1→π1(X)→π1(X,G)→G→1 over a finite subgroup correspond to fixed points (X ≠ S^2)
ideas.modern_name: topological/discrete analogue of the section conjecture; fixed points vs. sections of the equivariant fundamental group
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Smith theory, Nielsen realization, Kerckhoff 1983); anabelian formulation by Grothendieck (letter to Faltings 1983)
ideas.where_published: La Longue Marche (1981); letter to Faltings (1983) for the arithmetic analogue

ideas.what: Bijection between cone points of Y and conjugacy classes of maximal finite (cyclic) subgroups of the orbifold group, with the inclusion recovering the truncated loop map
ideas.modern_name: elliptic elements / maximal finite subgroups of Fuchsian groups correspond to cone points
ideas.where_published: possibly La Longue Marche, in the discussion of cartographic groups

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but classical statement: cone points correspond to maximal finite cyclic subgroups of the orbifold group, and splittings correspond to fixed points. It is a lemma in the cartographic-group programme of La Longue Marche and contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'pts fixes de G_0 opérant sur X': the subgroup letter is hard to read and may be G_a or G_0. Context suggests the fixed points of the subgroup over which one splits.
Interlinear insertion 'de π1(X,o)-conj.' reads as 'de π1(X,x)-conj.', qualifying 'ces classes'.
